readiness-low.label: Low readiness
readiness-low.summary: Your answers suggest you would benefit from building more meal rhythm and observation habits before starting a guided tracking plan.
keyPatterns: Meals often happen without a consistent daily rhythm
Planning ahead feels occasional rather than routine
Observation after meals is not yet a regular habit
firstFocusAreas: Establish one anchor meal time to build rhythm
Add a simple before-and-after meal check-in
Reduce the number of simultaneous changes you attempt
readiness-low.methodPositioning: Fine Diet starts with structure and observation — not restriction. When baseline habits are still forming, the first step is building a rhythm you can repeat, not tracking every detail.

page1.headline: You are building the foundation — and that is the right place to start.
body: Your answers point to a pattern many people recognize: daily eating does not yet have a steady rhythm, and observation habits are still forming.
That is not a failure. It means your next step is structure — not a full overhaul.
Before tracking intake productively, most people need a few repeatable anchors: roughly consistent meal times, simple meal composition, and brief check-ins after eating.
This result is a readiness snapshot, not a verdict. It tells us where support will help most.
snapshotBullets: Meal timing varies day to day
page1.meaningBody: You likely need the most structure before starting a guided plan. That is a normal starting point — not a reason to skip ahead.

page2.headline: Start with rhythm, not rules.
body: When baseline habits are still forming, the goal is repetition — not perfection.
Pick one anchor meal and protect its timing for two weeks. Add a 30-second check-in after one meal each day: How do I feel? What did I notice?
Avoid changing multiple variables at once. Structure first, then observation, then tracking.
stepBullets: Choose one anchor meal time and hold it for two weeks
Add a brief post-meal check-in once per day
Keep other changes minimal until rhythm feels familiar

page3.problemHeadline: Most plans skip the baseline step.
problemBody: Generic nutrition advice often assumes you already have meal rhythm, planning habits, and observation skills in place.
When those foundations are still forming, jumping straight into tracking can feel overwhelming — and the data is harder to interpret.
Fine Diet starts differently: structure first, observation second, guided tracking when you are ready.
tryBullets: Protect one anchor meal time for two weeks
Notice energy and comfort after one meal per day
Resist the urge to change everything at once
page3.tryCloser: Small, repeatable steps build the baseline that makes tracking useful.
page3.mechanismBodyTop: Rhythm reduces decision fatigue. Observation builds awareness without pressure.
page3.mechanismBodyBottom: When these habits feel familiar, tracking becomes a tool — not a burden.
methodBody: Fine Diet is built around observation and pattern recognition — not quick fixes or rigid rules.
Your readiness result helps us meet you where you are and sequence support appropriately.

readiness-building.label: Building readiness
readiness-building.summary: You have some baseline habits forming. A structured ramp into consistent observation and light tracking is a good next step.
keyPatterns: Some meal rhythm is present but not yet steady
Occasional planning and observation habits are emerging
Readiness to track is growing but not fully established
firstFocusAreas: Strengthen one or two anchor meal times
Make post-meal check-ins a daily habit
Begin light observation before full tracking
readiness-building.methodPositioning: Fine Diet meets you where your habits already are. When rhythm is forming, the focus is consistency — turning occasional good habits into repeatable ones.

page1.headline: You are building momentum — keep going.
body: Your answers show partial habits: some meal rhythm, some planning, some observation. That is real progress.
The opportunity now is consistency — turning occasional habits into a repeatable daily rhythm.
You do not need to be perfect. You need a pattern you can return to when life gets busy.
This result reflects readiness to ramp up — not readiness to skip the basics.
page1.meaningBody: You have partial habits but need consistency and rhythm before a full guided plan. That is a productive middle ground.

page2.headline: Turn occasional habits into daily rhythm.
body: Pick the habit that is closest to automatic and make it non-negotiable for two weeks.
Add a second anchor if the first feels stable. Keep check-ins brief — 30 seconds is enough.
When rhythm feels familiar, light tracking (even mental notes) becomes much more useful.
stepBullets: Lock in your strongest existing meal-time habit
Introduce light observation before full logging

problemBody: Many people stall because they try to perfect every meal instead of repeating a few good patterns.
When habits are forming, the win is showing up — not optimizing every detail.
Fine Diet helps you build rhythm first, then layer in guided observation and tracking when the foundation holds.
tryBullets: Make your best existing habit non-negotiable for two weeks
Add one new anchor only after the first feels automatic
Start a simple observation log before full tracking
page3.tryCloser: Steady repetition is what turns partial habits into baseline readiness.
page3.mechanismBodyTop: When meals follow a pattern, observation data becomes meaningful instead of noisy.
page3.mechanismBodyBottom: You are close — consistency is the bridge to guided tracking.
methodBody: Fine Diet sequences support to match your readiness. You are in the building phase — structure and observation come before full tracking.
Your result helps us recommend the right pace for your next step.

readiness-ready.label: Ready to start
readiness-ready.summary: Your meal rhythm and observation habits suggest you have enough baseline structure to begin a more guided Fine Diet plan.
keyPatterns: Planning and observation are regular habits
You feel ready to observe and log without overhauling everything
firstFocusAreas: Begin guided observation and light tracking
Use your existing rhythm as the foundation
Layer in Fine Diet Method sequencing at your pace
readiness-ready.methodPositioning: Fine Diet is designed for people who already have baseline structure. Your readiness result confirms you can start guided observation and tracking without rebuilding from scratch.

page1.headline: You have a solid baseline — you are ready to start.
body: Your answers show consistent meal rhythm, regular planning, and established observation habits.
That is the foundation Fine Diet is built on. You do not need to overhaul your routine before starting.
Your next step is guided observation and tracking — using your existing structure as the starting point.
This result confirms readiness, not perfection. You are ready to begin the Method at your pace.
page1.meaningBody: You have enough baseline structure to start a more guided plan. Observation and tracking can build on what you already do.

page2.headline: Start guided observation from where you are.
body: Your existing rhythm is an asset — use it as the foundation for tracking.
Begin with one week of observation logging. Notice patterns without changing everything at once.
Fine Diet Method sequencing will help you interpret what you observe and decide what to adjust.
stepBullets: Log meals and brief observations for one week
Keep your existing meal rhythm — do not rebuild it
Review patterns before making targeted changes

page3.problemHeadline: You do not need to start over.
problemBody: Many programs assume you need a reset before you can make progress. Your readiness result says otherwise.
You already have structure. The Fine Diet Method helps you use observation and pattern recognition to decide what to adjust — not to start from zero.
Guided tracking builds on your baseline, it does not replace it.
tryBullets: Begin a one-week observation log using your current rhythm
Note energy and comfort patterns without changing meals yet
Review your log before deciding on any adjustments
page3.tryCloser: Your baseline is the starting line — not something to fix first.
page3.mechanismBodyTop: Consistent rhythm makes tracking data meaningful. Observation turns data into insight.
page3.mechanismBodyBottom: Fine Diet helps you interpret patterns and sequence changes — not impose a one-size-fits-all plan.
methodBody: Fine Diet is observation-first nutrition guidance. You are ready to begin the guided pathway built on the structure you already have.
Your readiness result confirms you can start without a full reset.
